req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid URL
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter of /redirect-to is missing or malformed.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must return HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter is missing or malformed. Examining the source code (lines 572-644), the handler does `response.headers['Location'] = args['url'].encode('utf-8')` with no guard — if 'url' is absent, a KeyError is raised (which Flask converts to 500, not 400). This means the current implementation does NOT satisfy R-HTTPBIN-027 as written. Tests must probe: (1) positive path — valid url param yields 3xx redirect with correct Location header, (2) negative path — missing url param, (3) boundary — empty string url param, (4) malformed url param, (5) status_code boundary values (300, 399, 301, 302). Each test asserts exact status codes and header values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302_with_location
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /redirect-to?url=https://example.com is issued
trace: R-HTTPBIN-027 positive path: valid url yields redirect
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302_with_location():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=https://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'https://example.com'

test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302_with_location()
